name: dutch-minilm-l6-v2
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (config.json max_position_embeddings 512). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: bidirectional encoder (BERT), full attention, no causal mask
notes: ADDED 2026-10-31. Not a plain fine-tune: a Dutch student distilled from sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, transformer layers copied from the teacher and the embedding layer RE-INITIALISED on a new 30k Dutch WordPiece vocabulary, then MSE-distilled on parallel en-nl pairs. 22.5M params vs the teacher's 22.7M - not an identical tensor set. Card prints teacher and student in the same tables: STSb-multi-mt nl Spearman 0.7508 vs 0.5546, STS17 nl-en 0.7929 vs 0.2900. Read with care - the teacher is English-only and scored on Dutch, so the gap is mostly language adaptation. Licence Apache-2.0, repo created 2026-05-13.

benchmarks.name: STSb-multi-mt (nl) Spearman
benchmarks.config: Card table '| Model | Spearman | Pearson |': 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (teacher, English)' 0.5546 vs 'dutch-minilm-l6-v2 (student, Dutch)' 0.7508 (x100). 1,379 Dutch pairs, unseen in training. Caveat: the comparison is an English-only teacher scored on a Dutch test, so most of the gap is language adaptation, not better semantics.

benchmarks.name: STSb-multi-mt (nl) Pearson
benchmarks.config: Same table, Pearson 0.5474 teacher vs 0.7540 student (x100).
